current_example.title: Example: Computing the Volume of a Region Using a Change of Variables

q-161892.name: Question 1
q-161892.problem:
Consider the finite region $R$ in the $xyz$-space, given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,1\le \frac{y}{x}\le 2,\,1\le xy\le 3,\,0\le z\le xy+3\}.
$$

By performing the change of variables

$$
u=\frac{y}{x},\,v=xy,\,w=z-xy,
$$

the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}xyz\,dV
$$

can be written in terms of $u,$ $v,$ and $w$ as
q-161892.worked_solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To find the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=\frac{y}{x},\,v=xy,\,w=z-xy,
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v,w)\,:\,1\le u\le 2,\,1\le v\le 3,\,-v\le w\le 3\}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-\frac{y}{{x}^{2}} & \frac{1}{x} & 0 \\ y & x & 0 \\ -y & -x & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-\frac{y}{{x}^{2}} & \frac{1}{x} \\ y & x\end{aligned}| \\  & =-\frac{y}{x}-\frac{y}{x} \\  & =-\frac{2y}{x} \\  & =-2u\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}=-\frac{1}{2u}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}xyz\,dV & ={∭}_{Δ}v(w+v)\cdot |-\frac{1}{2u}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{v(w+v)}{2u}\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{-v}^{3}\frac{v(w+v)}{2u}\,dw\,dv\,du\end{aligned}
$$

T:[uvw]⟶[x(u,v,w)y(u,v,w)z(u,v,w)]

To find the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

∭Rf(x,y,z) dV=∭Δ f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))|∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w)|dudvdw

where ∂(x,y,z)∂(u,v,w) is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to T.

u=yx,v=xy,w=z−xy,

gives us the inverse function T−1, that is

T−1:[xyz]→[u(x,y,z)v(x,y,z)w(x,y,z)].

To find the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

q-39058.name: Question 2
q-39058.problem:
Consider the finite region $R$ in the $xyz$-space, given by 

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,\pi \le x+y\le 2\pi ,\,0\le y+z\le \pi ,\,0\le z\le 1\}.
$$

Given the change of variables

$$
u=x+y,\,v=y+z,\,w=z,
$$

which of the following could be the missing part of the expression below?

$$
{∭}_{R}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)\,dV={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}\bbox[3pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAAA}}\,dw\,dv\,du
$$
q-39058.worked_solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To find the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$ 

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=x+y,\,v=y+z,\,w=z,
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the required integral, we proceed in four steps: 

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v,w)\,:\,\pi \le u\le 2\pi ,\,0\le v\le \pi ,\,0\le w\le 1\}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

  

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}=1.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)\,dV & ={∭}_{Δ}\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\cdot |\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\cdot |1|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\,\,dw\,dv\,du\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the finite region $R$ in the $xyz$-space, given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,2\le x-y\le 3,\,1\le {x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\le 4,\,1\le z\le 2\}.
$$

By performing the change of variables

$$
u=x-y,\,v={x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,w=3z,

{∭}_{R}6z\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-y)\,dV
$$

q-161889.worked_solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To find the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=x-y,\,v={x}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,w=3z,
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v,w)\,:\,2\le u\le 3,\,1\le v\le 4,\,3\le w\le 6\}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 2x & -2y & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =3|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2x & -2y\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(-2y+2x) \\  & =6(x-y) \\  & =6u\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{6u}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}6z\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-y)\,dV & ={∭}_{Δ}2w\operatorname{ln}⁡u\cdot |-\frac{1}{6u}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{w\operatorname{ln}⁡u}{3u}\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}{\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{3}^{6}\frac{w\operatorname{ln}⁡u}{3u}\,dw\,dv\,du\end{aligned}
$$

q-39054.problem:
Consider the finite region $R$ in the $xyz$-space, given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,\frac{3\pi }{4}\le 2x+y\le \pi ,\,0\le y+z\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,-1\le z\le 1\}.
$$

Given the change of variables

$$
u=2x+y,\,v=y+z,\,w=z,
$$

which of the following could be the missing part of the expression below?

$$
{∭}_{R}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+y)\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)\,dV={\int }_{3\pi /4}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}\bbox[3pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAAA}}\,dw\,dv\,du
$$
q-39054.worked_solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To find the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=2x+y,\,v=y+z,\,w=z
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v,w)\,:\,\frac{3\pi }{4}\le u\le \pi ,\,0\le v\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,-1\le w\le 1\}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(1-0) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+y)\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)\,dV & ={∭}_{Δ}\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\cdot |\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\cdot |\frac{1}{2}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{3\pi /4}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}\,\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\,\,dw\,dv\,du\end{aligned}
$$

T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To find the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=x,\,v=xy,\,w=3z,
$$

 

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v,w)\,:\,1\le u\le 2,\,0\le v\le 2,\,0\le w\le 3\}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ y & x & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =3|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ y & x\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(x-0) \\  & =3x \\  & =3u.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{3u}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}({x}^{2}y+3xyz)\,dV & ={∭}_{Δ}(uv+vw)\cdot |\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,du\,dv\,dw \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}(uv+vw)\cdot |\frac{1}{3u}|\,du\,dv\,dw \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}\,\frac{1}{3}(v+\frac{vw}{u})\,\,dw\,dv\,du\end{aligned}
$$

By performing the change of variables

the triple integral ∭R(x2y+3xyz)dV can be written in terms of u, v, and w as

q-162140.problem:
Use the change of variables 

$$
u=x+{y}^{2},\,v=y+z,\,w=z
$$

to evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}(x+{y}^{2})^{9}z\,dV,
$$

 
where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x+{y}^{2}\le 1,\,0\le y+z\le 5,\,0\le z\le 4\}.
$$
q-162140.worked_solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=x+{y}^{2},\,v=y+z,\,w=z
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v,w)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 5,\,0\le w\le 2\}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

$$

$$
u=y+z,\,v=x+4z,\,w=2y

$$

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v,w)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,1\le v\le e,\,0\le w\le 2\}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(-1)(-1). \\  & =2.\end{aligned}

q-162183.name: Question 14
q-162183.problem:
Find the volume bounded by the region $R,$ given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,1\le y\le 3,\,-2\le x-z\le 0,\,1\le \frac{z-1}{y}\le 5\}.
$$
q-162183.worked_solution:
Recall that the volume of $R$ can be found as 

$$
V={∭}_{R}\text{d}V.
$$

Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required volume, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

The inequalities that define the region $R,$

$$
1\le y\le 3,\,-2\le x-z\le 0,\,1\le \frac{z-1}{y}\le 5,
$$

suggest that we use the change of variables

$$
u=y,\,v=x-z,\,w=\frac{z-1}{y}.
$$

This change of variables gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required volume, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v,w)\,:\,1\le u\le 3,\,-2\le v\le 0,\,1\le w\le 5\}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & -\frac{z-1}{{y}^{2}} & \frac{1}{y}\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(-1)^{1+2}|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{y}\end{aligned}| \\  & =\frac{1}{y} \\  & =\frac{1}{u}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}=u.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}dV & ={∭}_{Δ}1\cdot |u|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{1}^{5}u\,dw\,dv\,du \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}u\,du\cdot {\int }_{-2}^{0}dv\cdot {\int }_{1}^{5}dw \\  & ={[\frac{{u}^{2}}{2}]}_{u=1}^{u=3}\cdot [v]_{v=-2}^{v=0}\cdot [w]_{w=1}^{w=5} \\  & =(\frac{9}{2}-\frac{1}{2})\cdot (0-(-2))\cdot (5-1) \\  & =32.\end{aligned}
$$

q-162153.problem:
Find the volume bounded by the region $R,$ given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y+3z\le 2,\,1\le {z}^{3}\le 8\}.
$$
q-162153.worked_solution:
Recall that the volume of $R$ can be found as 

$$
V={∭}_{R}\text{d}V.
$$

Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required volume, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

The inequalities that define the region $R,$

$$
0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y+3z\le 2,\,1\le {z}^{3}\le 8,
$$

suggest that we use the change of variables

$$
u=x,\,v=y+3z,\,w={z}^{3}.
$$

This change of variables gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required volume, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & =\{(u,v,w)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,0\le v\le 2,\,1\le w\le 8\}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3{z}^{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 3{z}^{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (3{z}^{2})-3\cdot 0 \\  & =3{z}^{2} \\  & =3{w}^{2/3}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{3{w}^{2/3}}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}dV & ={∭}_{Δ}1\cdot |\frac{1}{3{w}^{2/3}}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{8}{w}^{-2/3}\,dw\,dv\,du \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}du\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}dv\cdot {\int }_{1}^{8}{w}^{-2/3}dw \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[u]_{u=0}^{u=2}\cdot [v]_{v=0}^{v=2}\cdot [3{w}^{1/3}]_{w=1}^{w=8} \\  & =(2-0)\cdot (2-0)\cdot ({8}^{1/3}-{1}^{1/3}) \\  & =(2-0)\cdot (2-0)\cdot (2-1) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
